title: What is Git? Why every developer needs it
analogy: resume_final_v2_REAL files; game checkpoints; Google Docs history; Git = camera, GitHub = Instagram
devops: push → Jenkins CI/CD; infra as code; rollbacks

title: Install & Configure Git (Win/Mac/Linux) + aliases
analogy: Name tag on every parcel you send (user.name / email); speed-dial = aliases
devops: Wrong email on commits breaks audit trails & GitHub contribution graph; CI bots have their own identity

title: What is a Git Repository? `git init` & the .git folder
analogy: A notebook with a hidden CCTV logbook (.git) that records every page change; delete the logbook = history gone
devops: Every microservice / Terraform module lives in its own repo

title: status, add & commit — the 3 areas of Git
analogy: Sending a courier: items on table (working dir) → packed box (staging) → shipped with tracking no. (commit)
devops: Small focused commits = easy code review & safe deploys

title: git log & git commit --amend — fix your last commit
analogy: Editing your last WhatsApp message vs. a sent letter
devops: Fixing a typo'd commit message before pushing; never amend pushed shared commits

title: .gitignore — never commit secrets again
analogy: Packing for a trip: don't pack your house keys (.env) or the whole kitchen (node_modules)
devops: Real incident type: AWS keys pushed to a public repo get abused within minutes → rotate keys

title: Branches: create, switch, rename, delete (+ checkout)
analogy: Parallel drafts of a speech; road lanes

title: Merging branches & fixing merge conflicts
analogy: Two people editing the same sentence of a shared doc
devops: Conflicts in config/YAML files during release merges

title: git restore — undo uncommitted changes
analogy: Ctrl+Z before you save; un-packing an item from the box
devops: Accidentally edited a prod config file locally — restore it

title: git reset — soft vs mixed vs hard
analogy: Rewinding a video: soft keeps the edit timeline, hard shreds the footage
devops: Squashing local WIP commits before a PR; danger of --hard

title: git revert — the safe undo for shared history
analogy: Bank reversal entry instead of tearing a page out of the ledger
devops: Rolling back a bad production release without rewriting history

title: git stash — save work-in-progress
analogy: Guests arrive: put the half-cooked curry in the fridge, serve them, then continue

title: What is GitHub? Remotes, clone & push
analogy: Google Drive for code; "origin" = home address
devops: Jenkins/GitHub Actions pull from the remote on every push

title: git fetch vs git pull (+ pull requests)
analogy: Fetch = checking your mailbox; pull = opening the letters and acting on them
devops: PR workflow: review + CI checks before merge to main

title: git rebase & squash — clean history like a pro (series finale)
analogy: Re-coupling your train carriages behind the newest engine
devops: Clean linear history on main; trunk-based dev in CI/CD; reflog to rescue
